final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape score (0.974) combined with near-neutral ESM-1v plausibility (0.95), uniquely satisfying both strong antibody escape and preserved replication fitness.
Very high escape (0.933) with a modestly positive plausibility signal (0.155), the best escape/fitness balance after K188E; charge-reversal in a variable gp120 region is a plausible escape mechanism.

Strong escape (0.897) retained as third choice despite low plm (0.022), since its escape gain exceeds all remaining candidates; fitness risk noted but alternatives (T277A, S332T) are worse on escape or equally weak on plausibility.

stop_reason.detail: Escape and fitness-proxy scores already produce a stable top-3 with clear margins; further evidence is unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Restores the N330 (HXB2 N332) high-mannose glycan sequon absent in BG505; glycan addition is a well-known antibody-shielding escape mechanism with minimal fitness cost.
Position 332 is at the N332 glycan supersite region of gp120; local mutations there plausibly modulate broadly neutralizing antibody binding while typically retaining Env function.
Escape (0.720) is lower than the top candidates and plm is weak (0.036); demoted.
Removes the V1 PNGS (N136-I137-T138), a classic escape route from glycan-dependent bNAbs in the trimer apex region.
V1 loop Asn substitution can alter glycosylation/antigenic surface; V1 is variable so fitness cost likely modest.
Strong escape (0.897) but very low plm (0.022) raises fitness concerns; retained at rank 3 as the next-best escape option among remaining candidates.
Charge reversal in the V2 apex (analogous to HXB2 K169 escape mutations) disrupts PG9/PG16-class quaternary antibody binding while keeping surface exposure.
Surface Lys in V2-proximal region; charge reversal is a classic escape mechanism at antibody contact surfaces.
Highest EVEscape (0.974) combined with near-neutral ESM-1v plausibility (0.95), uniquely satisfying both escape gain and replication-fitness preservation; promoted to rank 1.
Alternative removal of the V1 glycan sequon via the +2 Thr, less disruptive to the local backbone than mutating the Asn itself.
V1 loop Thr→Ala is conservative and may remove local O-glycan/shielding features affecting antibody recognition.
Lowest escape among mid-tier candidates (0.693) with negligible plm (0.015); dominated on both dimensions.

rejection.reason: Lowest escape among mid-tier candidates (0.693) with negligible plm (0.015); dominated on both dimensions.

history.rationale: Disrupts the conserved N275 glycan sequon near the V2/V3 base, altering glycan shielding recognized by apex-directed antibodies.
C2-adjacent surface Thr; conservative Ala swap likely tolerable and sits near neutralization epitopes, so worth prioritizing for phenotype scoring.
Decent escape (0.817) but near-zero plm (0.008) suggests fitness cost; demoted below N136D.
Charge reversal in the lysine-rich V2 strand C region may reduce binding of electrostatics-dependent apex antibodies.
V2-proximal charge reversal candidate; moderate prior for escape with possible fitness trade-off.
Very high escape (0.933) with modestly positive plm (0.155), the best escape/fitness balance after K188E; promoted to rank 2.
V3 crown (GPGQ arch) mutation disrupting V3-directed neutralizing antibodies; higher fitness risk, so lower confidence.
Escape 0.805 but plm ~0.0002 is the worst fitness proxy in the pool; a charge-introducing mutation at a Gly with such low plausibility is high-risk.

rejection.reason: Escape 0.805 but plm ~0.0002 is the worst fitness proxy in the pool; a charge-introducing mutation at a Gly with such low plausibility is high-risk.

history.rationale: Removes the V2 CNTS glycan sequon; bidirectional escape/shielding effects make outcome uncertain, flagged for tool evidence.
Potential glycan-site modulation in V2 vicinity; Asn→Asp is conservative in size but removes glycosylation motif only if part of NxS/T sequon.
Escape 0.817 matches T277A but plm is essentially zero (0.001); no advantage over retained candidates.
